name: linear-a-lexicon
description: Proposed readings of Linear A words, names and documents from Tom di Mino's Linear A Lexicon, each with its confidence tier, its evidence and any rival reading on record.

interface.longDescription:
The Linear A Lexicon (linear-a.ai) holds Tom di Mino's proposed readings of Linear A, the script of Minoan Crete, as an archaic Semitic language. Ask what a Linear A word is proposed to mean, who or what a name refers to, how a tablet or libation table reads, which words are compared with a Hebrew, Ugaritic or Akkadian form, or which words are spelt with given signs.

Every reading here is Tom di Mino's proposal, and every result says so: each reading comes with a confidence tier (Confirmed, Probable, Candidate or Speculative) and what that tier means, the scholar who first proposed it where one is on record, and any rival reading the entry marks. Each result links to the page on linear-a.ai that shows the same record, so a claim can be checked.

Limitations: it covers Linear A only, not Linear B, Cretan Hieroglyphic or the Phaistos Disc. It reads the published Lexicon and changes nothing. It gives the readings on record and composes no new Minoan text. Some transliterations are given by link to the site and not in the result.
capabilities: Look up a word's proposed reading and tier
Read a document with its proposed translation
List words, names and documents by filter
Find words compared with a form
Search the Lexicon and its wiki
defaultPrompt: What does the Linear A word KU-RO mean?
Translate the Linear A tablet HT 13.

positive.description: A word looked up by its transliteration is given as a proposal with its tier.
positive.prompt: Linear A Lexicon: what does KU-RO mean?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the proposed reading kull, 'total, sum', as a proposal, with its tier Confirmed and the caveat that Confirmed fixes the word's function and not its etymology, the first proposer on record, any rival reading the entry marks, and the linear-a.ai link.

positive.description: A document is read with its proposed translation and a link to its page.
positive.prompt: Translate the Linear A tablet HT 13.
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the transliteration where the edition serves it or the link to the site's page where it does not, and the translation as a proposed translation with its tier, and links the document's page.

positive.description: Words compared with a Semitic form are listed as the Lexicon's comparisons.
positive.prompt: Which Linear A words are compared with Hebrew peten?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the Lexicon's words compared with that form, each with its proposed reading and tier, presented as the Lexicon's comparisons, with links.

positive.description: Words are found by the signs they end in.
positive.prompt: Which Linear A words end in TE?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists word forms of the corpus ending in the sign TE, the most attested first, with the count, and says which forms were not searched if the result says so.

positive.description: Words are listed by confidence tier, with what the tier means.
positive.prompt: List the Confirmed readings in the Linear A Lexicon.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the words whose tier is Confirmed, with each proposed reading and meaning, states what Confirmed means, and links the list.

negative.description: Linear B is outside the Lexicon, which covers Linear A only.
negative.prompt: Translate this Linear B tablet: PY Ta 641.
negative.expected_behavior: Gives no Lexicon reading for the tablet and says the Lexicon covers Linear A only.

negative.description: Every tool reads the published Lexicon and none writes to it, so an entry cannot be changed from a conversation.
negative.prompt: Change the Linear A Lexicon's entry for KU-RO so that it reads 'king'.
negative.expected_behavior: Changes nothing and says the Lexicon is read-only; may show the entry as it stands and where a revision can be suggested.

negative.description: No tool gives weather; all eighteen read the Lexicon.
negative.prompt: What is the weather in Heraklion today?
negative.expected_behavior: No Linear A Lexicon tool is called.

review.commerce_description: The Linear A Lexicon sells nothing and processes no payments.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: eighteen read-only tools over the Linear A Lexicon's words, names, documents, roots, signs, bibliography, wiki and statistical tests.
